command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
[ -f "$change/proposal.md" ] || { echo "$record names change '$change_name', but $change/proposal.md does not exist - write the change there, or name the active change the task is about"; exit 1; }
verdict=$(sed -n 's/^Verdict:[[:space:]]*//p' "$record" | head -1)
if [ "$verdict" != "no-blocking-dependencies" ]; then
  echo "the change record's verdict is '$verdict'; the only verdict that finishes this stage is 'no-blocking-dependencies'."
  echo "If the change IS blocked, do not finish the round: write the dependency chain to the path in \$GNOMISH_DECISION_FILE as {\"question\": \"...\", \"options\": [\"...\"]}, delete $record and end your turn."
  exit 1
fi

findings.message: Handoff H1 (tasks.md 6.2 and the `## Human follow-up` H1 bullet) does not tell the operator which glossary patch to apply first. The new `H1-glossary-handle-drag.patch` is made with `git diff -U0` and changes lines 6–7 of `docs/glossary/time-selection.md` (the Day track and Handle entries). The still-unapplied `openspec/changes/archive/2026/10/2026-10-30-fix-day-track-handle-overlap-and-end-of-day/handoff/H1-glossary-track-end.patch` (hunk `@@ -5,11 +5,12 @@`) uses those same two lines, unchanged, as context (`All handles stand at the same position.` / `Dragging it, or tapping the track, selects a time.`). If the new patch goes in first, the earlier one fails to apply. Task 6.2 only checks the order track-end first, then the new patch, but the README's **Apply** is just `git apply --unidiff-zero <path>` and the follow-up bullet says nothing about order. handoff.md requires '**Apply:** the exact command, run from the repository root'. Either state the order (apply H1-glossary-track-end.patch first) in the Apply line and the follow-up bullet, or build the patch against the glossary with that patch already applied.
